Autonomy and the rulebook

An optional layer that remembers how you answer the questions the loop parks on, and lets it earn the right to answer the repeated ones itself, always with a window in which you can say no.

On this page
  • What the rulebook is
  • The parts, and turning them on
  • Autonomy levels
  • The applier and the veto window
  • What always parks for a person
  • Reading a decision record
  • Keys and defaults

Most people only need

  • Everything here is off. A fresh repository does not use the rulebook.
  • Below level 3 it only records your answers and recommends. It never decides.
  • Dangerous actions (the irreversible kind) are never answered for you, at any level.
  • Your answer always wins over an automatic one, and an owner's no after an apply puts the goal back.

When the loop parks a goal because it needs a decision, you answer through /sigma-unpark, or approve through /sigma-promote. With the rulebook on, that answer is stored as a decision record in the repository. When enough answers of one kind in one area agree, that pair earns a higher autonomy level. At low levels the loop only records and recommends. At the top two levels, and only if you open the applier, it may answer a question nobody answered in time, using a rule an owner approved, and tell you it did.

What the rulebook is

  • Opt-in, in parts. The rulebook block in .sdlc/config.json has several parts, and each opens only when its own enabled is the JSON boolean true. The text "true", "yes" and the number 1 all stay off. A wrong-typed block closes the whole rulebook, and /sigma-doctor names the key.
  • A kind is the class of a parked question, declared by the agent that parks it (for example dependency, failing_check, irreversible). Without a declared kind a park is not learnable.
  • An area is the first area:<x> label on the issue in sorted order, else repo for the whole repository.
  • A rule says: for this kind in this area, recommend this option. It starts as proposed; an owner's approval makes it count (unless rulebook.rules.auto_approve, false by default, lets the watcher approve rules as the first configured owner), and a rule edited by hand after approval stops counting.
  • Records and rules describe the repository and its areas, never a person. A rule with a person field is invalid.

The parts, and turning them on

PartKeyWhat it addsDefault
Recordsrulebook.recordsStores each answer as a record and counts them.off
Hard stopsrulebook.hard_stopsClassifies concrete actions and parks the dangerous ones.off
Autonomyrulebook.autonomyDerives levels from records.off
Rulesrulebook.rulesA committed file of approved rules, .sdlc/rulebook.json.off
Drift judgerulebook.driftJudges a parked question against reference documents, shadow only; it never changes a label or parks.off
Applierrulebook.autonomy.applierLevels 3 and 4: answers an unanswered question.off

Open them in order and stop wherever you are comfortable. A repository scaffolded earlier does not receive the block: copy it from the installed template with every enabled still false, then run /sigma-doctor. If the repository is public, set rulebook.records.repo_visibility to "public" before opening anything. Name the people who may approve rules in rulebook.autonomy.owners; if it is left out, spend_approval.approvers is used, and if both are empty, owner confirmation is refused. The applier is last, and it needs the ledger watcher running, because the watcher runs its tick.

Autonomy levels

A level from 0 to 4 is derived for each kind and area. It is never stored.

LevelAnswers neededAgreement neededWhat the loop may do
0fewer than 10noneAsk every time.
110noneAsk; counting has started.
2300.90Ask, with an approved rule offered as a recommendation.
3600.95The applier may act, and says so in a comment every time.
43000.99The applier may act silently, only for kinds you list in allow_silent on an owner-approved rule.
  • Agreement is how often the rulebook's pick matched the person's. When machines disagree the lowest level wins, so disagreement never raises trust.
  • Imported evidence from past work counts toward levels 1 and 2 and never above level 2.
  • A veto (an owner's no after an applied answer) drops the kind one level. Three vetoes in a row, or twenty in all, pause the kind at level 0.
  • Hard-stop kinds are capped at level 2, whatever the evidence.

The applier and the veto window

The applier is the one part that answers for a person. It is a separate gate and runs as one more timed call in the ledger watcher's tick. Closed, it spawns nothing and writes nothing. It applies an answer only when all of these hold: nobody has answered, the window has passed (window_minutes, default 1440, one day), the kind is not a hard-stop kind, the derived level is at least 3, exactly one approved rule matches, and fewer than max_auto_applied_per_day (default 3) were applied in the last 24 hours.

It then does one atomic gesture (an unpark, or a promote), writes the record, and posts a comment naming the rule. An owner's exact no inside the window puts the goal back and lowers the level. A person's own gesture on the same issue always wins.

The tick writes a heartbeat. The doctor reads a tick as dead when the heartbeat is missing or older than stale_after_intervals watch intervals, which defaults to 3. A dead tick is harmless: the goal simply stays parked. If another machine's evidence is ahead of your checkout, the tick acts on nothing and the doctor says HELD with the reason; pull the default branch to clear it.

What always parks for a person

  • The irreversible kind: it is never applied for you, a rule never matches it, and its level stays at or below 2. That cap is fixed and not configurable.
  • An undeclared kind: it opens no ask.
  • Held goals from the scope and ownership gates (scope_hold, owner_hold): the automatic sweep never resumes them.
  • In a chain, a paid step is always put to a person and never defaulted.
  • With rulebook.hard_stops open: a concrete action classified as spend, destroy, rewrite_history, production_change, send_outside or access_secrets. An action it cannot classify counts as dangerous, not permitted. Without that part, the same five-way list (deploy, delete, overwrite, spend, migrate) is an instruction to the agent that no code checks.

The rulebook also never acts silently unless the kind is on your allow_silent list; even then every fifth silent-eligible apply (spot_check_one_in) still comments.

Reading a decision record

A record is one small JSON file in .sdlc/decisions, about 1 KB, created exclusively so parallel worktrees add distinct files and never edit a shared one. Each gesture also posts one comment on the issue carrying the same record id.

FieldWhat it tells you
id, timeWhich record, and when.
gestureWhat was done: unpark, keep-parked, promote, demote, an acknowledgement, or an apply.
qkind, areaThe kind of question and the area it was answered in.
choice, reasonThe option taken and why. These are the only free-text fields.
howhuman (a person's gesture), autonomous (the sweep or the applier) or imported (read back from past work).
issue, rule_idThe issue, and the rule involved when there was one.

To audit what the loop did on its own, look for how: autonomous. On a public repository, set the visibility key so choice text is not written where it would be exposed.

Keys and defaults

KeyDefault
rulebook.records.enabled, rulebook.autonomy.enabled, rulebook.rules.enabled, rulebook.hard_stops.enabled, rulebook.drift.enabled, rulebook.autonomy.applier.enabledfalse
rulebook.autonomy.levels.l1_min_answers to l4_min_answers10, 30, 60, 300
rulebook.autonomy.levels.l2_agreement to l4_agreement0.9, 0.95, 0.99
rulebook.autonomy.applier.window_minutes1440
rulebook.autonomy.applier.max_auto_applied_per_day3
rulebook.autonomy.applier.spot_check_one_in5
rulebook.autonomy.applier.allow_silent[]
rulebook.autonomy.applier.stale_after_intervals3
rulebook.autonomy.veto_pause_consecutive, veto_pause_total3, 20
rulebook.rules.reask_days90
rulebook.records.repo_visibility"private"
rulebook.hard_stops.classes.tamper_oversight, unvetted_executionfalse

Cost. Records, levels and rules are plain files and cost no model calls. The drift judge calls a model only with a model name and a positive daily ceiling set. The importer reads past work with a table classifier by default; a model classifier is a separate setting with its own per-call and per-run budget. Spend ceilings, weekly and monthly, default to unset.
